title: AI Guard policies: detector settings, policy control rules, first-match order, applications and testing

prose.text: An AI Guard policy is a set of detector settings; it applies to traffic only through a policy control rule that matches it. Both halves are covered here.

prose.label: Policy control.

checks.do: The rules above the expected one in policy control order, since evaluation stops at the first match.

That the rule is enabled and its criteria match the traffic: provider and model, account type, users or groups for user rules; applications, credentials, application groups, source IPs or custom headers for application rules.
The detector's Action (Block, Detect or Allow) and threshold in the policy; Detect only flags.
Run the policy through Policy Testing with the same provider credential and model before relying on it.

policy-is-detectors.statement: A policy is set by enabling detectors on prompts and responses; a tenant can have several policies, apply one per app, several to one app, or one to several apps.

quotes: You set a policy by enabling one or more included detectors on prompts and responses.
Every policy is a guardrail, and you can set up multiple policies, define and apply a policy per app, apply multiple policies to one app, or apply a policy to multiple apps.

detector-settings.statement: Most detectors share Enabled (on by default), Severity, Threshold (the lower it is, the more strictly AI Guard activates the policy) and Action: Allow lets the prompt proceed, Block blocks it, Detect flags it as detected, and some detectors also offer Disabled.

quotes: Most prompt detectors share the following configuration options:
Enabled: Enables the prompt detector and is on by default.
Severity: Corresponds to the severity icons in the Prompt Detectors column on the Policies page.
Threshold: The lower the threshold setting, the more strict AI Guard is with activating the policy (i.e., allowing, blocking, or detecting the prompt).
Allow allows the prompt to proceed, Block blocks the prompt, and Detect flags the prompt as detected.
Some detectors include a Disabled option to ensure what is disabled is not covered under that category's detections.

pii-name-disabled.statement: In the PII detector the Person's name category defaults to Disabled.

quotes: In the PII detector, the Person's name category is defaulted to Disabled.

ten-limit.statement: Competition and Topic accept at most 10 entries at a time in a single policy.

quotes: Only 10 can be set at a time for a single policy.
evidence.after: Competition: Includes a Competitors category where you enter your specific competitor names.

quotes: Only 10 can be set at a time for a single policy.
evidence.after: Topic: Includes the ability to add multiple custom topics to add to your policy.

control-binding.statement: A policy configuration is applied by attaching it through policy control to an LLM provider, user or user group; policy controls are evaluated top to bottom and evaluation stops at the first match.

quotes: After you create an AI Guard policy configuration, you can then attach it to an LLM provider, user, or user group by adding policy control.
Policies are evaluated from top-to-bottom and the evaluation will stop after matching the first policy.

user-control-fields.statement: A user policy control needs a rule name, a policy configuration, a rule order and a rule status (enabled or disabled), and at least one match criterion among LLM provider and models (with Account Type when Organization Restrictions are on), users and user groups.

quotes: Rule Name: Enter a name for the policy match.
Policy Configuration: From the drop-down menu, select a policy you previously created.
Rule Order: Enter a number for the order in which you want the policy match applied.
Rule Status: Select whether you want the rule to be enabled or disabled.
Match Criteria: At least one match criteria must be defined:
Account Type: If Organization Restrictions are enabled, select Enterprise, Personal, or Both.
Users: Click the drop-down menu and select the users you want to include with the match criteria.
User Groups: Click the drop-down to select the groups you want to include in the match criteria.

criteria-types.statement: In the API a match rule's criteria have one of three types: `APPLICATION` targets LLM applications (optionally specific application credentials), application groups, LLM providers, source IPs and optional custom request headers; `DAS_APPLICATION` targets DAS applications the same way without providers; `USER` targets Zscaler users and user groups, optionally narrowed by LLM provider.

expect.description: Polymorphic base for match-rule criteria; the `type` discriminator selects the concrete subtype (APPLICATION, USER, or DAS_APPLICATION).
Match criteria targeting LLM applications, application groups, LLM providers, source IPs, and optional custom request headers.
Selects a specific LLM application (by id or name) and, optionally, particular application credentials.
Match criteria targeting DAS applications, identified by LLM applications, application groups, source IPs, and optional custom request headers.
Match criteria targeting specific Zscaler users and user groups, optionally narrowed by LLM provider.

match-rule-references.statement: Creating a match rule through the API requires the detection policy and any LLM applications it names to exist already; otherwise the request is rejected with a message naming the missing item.

expect.description:
Creates a new detection policy match rule with priority ordering. The detection policy and any
LLM applications the rule refers to must already exist; if a referenced policy or application
cannot be found, the request is rejected with a message that names the missing item.

no-match-unapplied.statement: A policy configuration applies to traffic only through an enabled policy control that matches it first; a policy with no such rule, a disabled rule, or a rule below an earlier match is not applied to that traffic.
no-match-unapplied.conditions: Follows from first-match evaluation and the rule status field; no page describes the failure case.

enable-disable-match-rules.statement: Enabling or disabling a detection policy through the API turns every match rule that references it on or off, and the response lists those rules with their new state; disabling does not delete the policy.

expect.description: Result of enabling or disabling a detection policy. Enabling or disabling a policy turns every match rule that references it on or off; the response lists those match rules with their new state rather than the full policy.
Disables the detection policy without deleting it.

ai-applications.statement: AI applications such as chatbots are added while configuring AI Guard so a policy can be applied to them; they can be grouped into application groups; a DaaS application carries API keys and a Proxy application an identity broker.

quotes: Adding an AI application (such as a chatbot) needs to be done while configuring AI Guard. Once added, an AI Guard policy can be configured and applied to it.
Applications: From the drop-down menu, select the applications you want to group together.

testing.statement: Policy Testing, available once an LLM provider, its credentials and a policy exist, sends a prompt through a chosen provider credential, policy and LLM model and shows what was allowed or blocked together with the prompt and response without guardrails.

quotes: After adding a large language model (LLM) provider, LLM provider credentials, and a policy to AI Guard, you can test your policy to make sure it is working to your satisfaction.
Provider Credential: From the drop-down menu, select an LLM credential.
Policy: From the drop-down menu, select a policy you want to test.
LLM Model: From the drop-down menu, select the LLM model you want to use.
In addition to the policy test showing you what is allowed or blocked, it also shows you the prompt and response without guardrails.

no-match-default.title: What AI Guard does with traffic that no policy control matches
no-match-default.detail: No captured page says whether unmatched traffic is allowed uninspected, inspected by a default policy, or blocked. The ZIA integration names AllUsersGroup as the default user group (ai-security.ai-guard.zia-integration:users-appear), which does not say what policy applies to it.
no-match-default.blocks: answers on traffic outside every policy control
